name: Barbell Shrug
description: The barbell shrug is an isolation exercise for the upper trapezius, performed by elevating the shoulders while holding a heavy barbell at arm's length. It is the primary direct exercise for developing upper trap thickness and neck size, and is commonly used by strength athletes to improve grip strength and upper back robustness.

execution.starting_position: Stand upright holding a barbell at arm's length in front of the thighs with a pronated or mixed grip. Feet shoulder-width apart, spine neutral.
execution.setup_instructions: Set up like a deadlift start position but keep the bar at thigh height. Use lifting straps for heavy sets to prevent grip from being the limiting factor.
steps: Elevate the shoulders straight upward as high as possible, contracting the upper trapezius.
Hold the top position for one second.
Lower the shoulders back down in a controlled manner to full depression.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you shrug up. Inhale as you lower.
common_mistakes: Rolling the shoulders forward or backward — shrug straight up
Using body swing or bend to generate momentum
Not achieving full range of motion in both directions
safety_considerations: Avoid heavy shrugs if you have neck or cervical spine issues
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full elevation of the shoulders at the top, full depression at the bottom.
coaching_cues: Shrug straight up — not forward, not back, just up
Try to touch your ears with your shoulders at the top
